facts.text: Hamilton Heights takes its name from Alexander Hamilton, who lived in the area at Hamilton Grange.
The neighborhood’s historic district was designated in 1974, preserving fine apartment houses along Amsterdam Ave between 140th and 145th Streets.
The 137th Street–City College and 145th Street subway stops opened with the IRT Broadway–Seventh Avenue Line in 1904, linking the area to downtown.
During the Harlem Renaissance, artists like Count Basie and Paul Robeson called Hamilton Heights home, making it a cultural hotspot.
The Carnegie library that opened in 1907 still stands and was renovated in 1975, now listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
The neighborhood borders 135th Street to the south, Riverside Drive to the west, 155th Street to the north, and Edgecombe and Saint Nicholas Avenues to the east.
